frontier_coordinate: R-111 proves the exact stationary scalar k:2k square-first inequality for every q and amplitude on both degenerate covariance faces. On the genuinely mixed face it gives the exact I_0 radial normalizer, positive fixed-shape projective limiting gap and first inverse-amplitude correction, exact phase-floor high-q reduction, rigorous factorized tails, and three exact method no-gos. new_claim_criteria: The statement is mathematically independent of the current parent objective.
The scope and falsifier remain meaningful when cited without the parent proof diary.
The result has its own reproducible verification package or an explicitly staged package plan.
The result is intended to be a durable external citation target.
The unit is not merely a lemma, route comparison, obstruction, counterexample, or next gate inside an active claim.

The score identity is expectation-only and cannot replace the raw Wick coordinate inside an exponential. The narrowed successor is one raw complete same-root diagonal-to-decoupled or direct signed cluster estimate retaining a predictable square-first covariance cost, Cameron--Martin mean, cross-mode baseline/current, trace, future feedback, rational recovery, all visits, the random-W raw forest, and exactly one source/sextic ownership ledger. Static covariance norms and any uncentred universal nonlinear tangent-square normalizer fail on exact fixtures. In a stationary scalar two-frequency k:2k whole-output model, the exact moments yield a strict right-small-q margin and two quadrature orders retain positive finite-point signs, but no convergence, bare all-q theorem, or full A1 embedding is claimed. Its architecture-sharp pointwise payment is nonsummable for the declared positive-density bounded-multiplicity production allocation. R-111 proves that scalar inequality for every q on both degenerate covariance faces and reduces the mixed face to a positive fixed-shape projective boundary, exact high-q floor, rigorous tails, and a residual compact core; quadratic-Bessel domination, sign-blind conditional scalar tensorization, and monotone tilted variance are retired.
